title: Article 135 — Jurisdiction and powers of the Federal Court under existing law to be exercisable by the Supreme Court

content.overview: Article 135 provides that until Parliament by law otherwise provides, the Supreme Court shall also have jurisdiction and powers with respect to any matter to which the provisions of Article 133 or Article 134 do not apply if jurisdiction and powers in relation to that matter were exercisable by the Federal Court immediately before the commencement of the Constitution under any existing law.
content.glance: SC inherits Federal Court’s jurisdiction under existing law where Arts 133/134 do not apply, until Parliament otherwise provides.
content.study:
Article 135 is a transitional/continuance provision ensuring that jurisdiction and powers of the Federal Court under pre-Constitution existing law continue in the Supreme Court where Articles 133 and 134 do not cover the matter, until Parliament legislates otherwise.

Examination: Federal Court continuity; residual until parliamentary law; link Arts 133–134.

sections.heading: Key rule
sections.body: Until Parliament by law otherwise provides, the SC has the jurisdiction and powers that the Federal Court had under existing law immediately before commencement, in matters not covered by Arts 133 or 134.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What does Article 135 provide?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Article 135 provides that until Parliament by law otherwise provides, the Supreme Court shall also have jurisdiction and powers with respect to any matter to which Articles 133 or 134 do not apply, if jurisdiction and powers in relation to that matter were exercisable by the Federal Court immediately before the commencement of the Constitution under any existing law.

examTips: Federal Court jurisdiction continued in SC until Parliament provides otherwise.

keyTakeaways: Art 135: SC inherits residual Federal Court jurisdiction under existing law.
